authoringNotes.status: Approximate centreline from OpenStreetMap ways, checked against the GSI 1974–1978 aerial layer (gazo1); the 1979–1990 layers have no coverage here. Not surveyed or native-qualified.
authoringNotes.sprintRoute: Umagaeshi junction → Ōya-bashi over the Daiya → Chichinoki-bashi → curves い to ね (1–20) → Kurokamidaira (れ) → Akechidaira ropeway car park, the 1986 top of the uphill one-way section. Driven uphill, the only legal direction since 7 October 1965. The last ~200 m above the junction with the 1932 lake road may have carried two-way traffic in 1986 (unconfirmed); uphill is legal either way.
authoringNotes.topologyReason: Sprint. The Second Irohazaka is uphill-only and the First downhill-only, so a loop needs the 6.5 km First as a second leg (about 16 km in all) and cannot fit 5:00. The 1986 continuation from Akechidaira to the lake was the two-way 1932 road through the old Akechi and Hakuun tunnels (closed 1994); it would add about 2.1 km, beyond the slower cars' budget.
authoringNotes.elevationsAndWidths: Elevations: GSI 1 m laser DEM every 20 m, with bridge decks and a 1994 bypass-structure artefact interpolated, then a ±45 m moving average (864 → 1,275 m). Half-width 4.0 m throughout (an 8 m two-lane carriageway with shoulders; not a 1986 survey value), widening to 5.0 m into the car park. Hairpin widening is not modelled: the native wall solver stops a car hugging the outside wall wherever the corridor narrows.
authoringNotes.kanaCurves: Each kana curve is a named control point at the tightest radius within 30 m of its OSM guidepost (2023 sign positions; the 1986 positions are assumed unchanged). Eleven kana curves plus Kurokamidaira (curve れ) are gates.
authoringNotes.cornerGeometry: Quadratic tangent trims at the 30% cap. Vertices lie on a ±3 m smoothed OSM line every ≤32° of heading change, ≤110 m apart, chord error ≤2 m; edges are then split until no vertex turns more than 40°. The compiled centreline stays within 2.3 m of the OSM line; the tightest 20 m-averaged radius is about 13 m (curve た). At the engine’s 5 m cells curve た compiled to 8.4 m, so it was redrawn (see hairpins).
authoringNotes.timing: targetMs is a scripted test driver at 75% of the native yaw-limited corner speed: 3:05.1 on the Tokyo 8-car graph used only as a motion engine. 45% took 4:36; the 300 s cap (86.2 km/h average) falls near 43%. The repository practice AI (streetDriver) did not finish: it pins itself to the walls at the first loop and the hairpins.
authoringNotes.musicCues: Placeholder asset and digest. Cues mark the start, curve い, the staircase from へ, the Nantai view at Kurokamidaira and curve ね, timed from the 3:05 test run.
authoringNotes.notForProfile: Not admitted to any live profile. Current RaceV1 accepts only 3 tracks and 5,400 ticks.
authoringNotes.hairpins: On 2026-10-29 curve た was redrawn as a 12.5 m minimum-radius (Dubins) path between anchors on its own legs. Its trace was an 8.4 m bend at the engine’s 5 m cell scale, which a car could take only at 37 km/h and only on the very outside line; it now allows 79 km/h there. The gate curve-ta moved 8.6 m to the nearest new point, and the route is 18 m shorter (7.169 km), so the kana boards from た on moved with it. Re-sampling the shorter route shifts the other hairpins’ 5 m readings by up to 3 km/h. The original trace is world/research/routes/irohazaka-1986.trace.json.

sources.usedFor: Second Irohazaka centreline (oneway, two lanes) to Akechidaira, with ways 426182285, 426182284 (Ōya-bashi), 986511510 and 986511511 (Chichinoki-bashi).
Curve guideposts い (ref 1) to ね (ref 20), nodes 6704987956–6704987975: kana order and positions.
Visually compared 1974–1978 aerials with the OSM alignment: junction, all hairpins and Akechidaira match. gazo2/3/4 return no tiles here.
GSI elevation API (1 m laser DEM): climb profile and line-of-sight checks.
Toll from 1 Oct 1954; Second opened 7 Oct 1965 Umagaeshi–Akechidaira; free from 1 Oct 1984; Akechidaira bypass built 1989–30 Mar 1994; old Akechi and Hakuun tunnels closed.
1954 rebuild, 1965 Second Irohazaka with 20 curves, 48 curves in all, 15.8 km.
The uphill Second carries the first twenty kana; First 6.5 km, Second 9.5 km.
Until September 2019, uphill-only from Umagaeshi to the Akechidaira ropeway car park and two-way beyond.
The 2 km above Akechidaira stayed two-way until the permanent one-way order of 1 Oct 2019.
Opened 3 Nov 1933, removed 1943, reopened 5 Oct 1950, Nikko Kotsu from 1 Apr 1985; rest house in the former funicular station, demolished 2017–2018.
Funicular Umagaeshi–Akechidaira 28 Aug 1932–1 Apr 1970; Akechidaira–Chūgūshi motor road 1932; Umagaeshi tram closed 1968.
Kegon Falls lip collapse in October 1986 (about 4,000 m³) and the 1976 left-bank collapse.
Curve signs installed March 1995 and replaced May 2023, so neither design is the 1986 one.
Nantai-san 2,486 m since a 2003 GSI survey; 2,484 m was the accepted height in 1986.
